elements.element: Renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement, OR the Agreement auto-renews for 12-month terms
elements.evidence: 'shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof' — the term is evergreen with no renewal mechanic, so the auto-renewal condition is demonstrably absent and no renewal language need be invented.

elements.element: Customer opt-out of automatic renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: 'either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice' — no auto-renewal exists; exit right is already shorter than 30 days and benefits Company.
No renewal date exists ('continue until terminated'), so the reminder condition is absent.

elements.element: Price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: 'any such increase shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI over the preceding twelve (12) months and three percent (3%)'

elements.element: Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: 'shall continue until terminated' — no automatic renewal and no non-renewal notice window; condition absent (official pattern simply found no number).
'shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI ... and three percent (3%)' — within the 5% ceiling.

offending_extra_words: no more than once in any twelve (12) month period
No rate change shall apply to any Statement of Work then outstanding without Company's prior written consent.
reasons: Substantively the locked preferred level is complete: the rate-change sentence now carries the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap, and the renewal/notice-window elements are conditionally absent because the term is evergreen with a 15-day mutual exit rather than auto-renewing.

Minimality fails. The edit expands 13 words to 66 (ratio 5.08) and changes 86% of the characters, when inserting the cap alone (e.g. 'Contractor may change rates upon 30 days prior written notice to Company, provided any increase shall not exceed the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent (3%).') would suffice.

Two additions go beyond what the rule requires: an annual frequency limit ('no more than once in any twelve (12) month period') and a new consent gate for outstanding Statements of Work — extra protections not part of the renewal price-cap position.

Intent is preserved: the evergreen term, invoicing detail and 15-day termination right are untouched, and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is created. Minor note only: 'CPI' is used without a defined index or source, which is worth pinning down.
